CT.name: Connecticut

notice.text: Call at least 2 full days (not weekends or holidays) and not more than 30 days before digging.

start.text: Call no more than 30 days before work starts.

life.text: A ticket expires 30 days from the day it is given.

CT.renew: Past 30 days you need a new ticket. Call it in at least 2 full working days before the old one ends.
CT.emergency: Emergency work: call the center right away, by phone as soon as you can.

trench.text: Federal OSHA covers private crews here: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

CT.osha_name: Federal OSHA for private employers (state plan covers public workers only)

sources.what: One-call center directory, March 2026 (cross-check of center names)

DE.name: Delaware

notice.text: Call at least 3 and not more than 12 business days before digging.

start.text: Call no more than 12 business days before work starts.

life.text: A ticket is good for 12 business days after it is sent. On day 13 it expires.

DE.renew: Get an update, remark or new ticket before day 13. The app’s Renew-by date uses the first-call wait: no source names a day.
DE.tol_text: 24 inches from the outside of the facility.
DE.white_text: White lining is highly recommended when the exact spot can’t be described.
DE.emergency: Emergency: the wait does not apply. Notify the center at the earliest moment.

trench.text: Federal OSHA covers private crews here: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

sources.what: Del. Code Title 26, ch. 8, subch. I (802, 806)

FL.name: Florida

notice.text: Call at least 2 full business days before digging (10 for underwater work).

life.text: Ticket information is good for 30 calendar days after you give it.

FL.renew: Past 30 days, call in again. Leave out the areas that are finished. The app’s Renew-by date uses the first-call wait: no source names a day.
FL.tol_text: Lines are marked within 24 inches of either side. Hand dig, pothole or vacuum inside the tolerance zone.

trench.text: Federal OSHA covers private crews here: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

IL.name: Illinois

notice.text: Give notice not less than 2 days and not more than 10 days before digging (law from Jan 1, 2025).

start.text: Give notice no more than 10 days before work starts.

life.text: A notice is good for 25 days from the request. The law’s “day” skips weekends, JULIE holidays and the day of the notice.

IL.renew: Ask JULIE for an extension before the 25 days end, and not before the 20th day. It adds 25 days to the old end date. Pre-mark again if you want new marks.

trench.text: Federal OSHA covers private crews here: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

IL.osha_name: Federal OSHA for private employers (state plan covers public workers only)

sources.what: 220 ILCS 50/2: “Day”, “Extension”, “Normal notice request” (text current to Jan 1, 2025)

KS.name: Kansas

notice.text: Call at least 2 full working days and not more than 20 calendar days before the start date.

start.text: Call no more than 20 calendar days before work starts.

life.text: A notice is good for 20 calendar days after the start date. The app counts from the first legal dig day.

KS.renew: Update the notice to go on. An update is good for 20 calendar days after its own start date. The app’s Renew-by date uses the first-call wait: no source names a day.
KS.white_text: White-line the site when the operator asks.
KS.emergency: The notice rule does not apply in an emergency.

trench.text: Federal OSHA covers private crews here: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

MO.name: Missouri

notice.text: Call at least 2 and not more than 10 working days before digging.

start.text: Not started within 10 working days: ask for a relocate.

life.text: A notice is good until 11:59 PM, 21 calendar days from the start date (law of Aug 28, 2025). The app counts from the first legal dig day.

MO.renew: Not started within 10 working days: ask for a relocate first. Past 21 days you need a new ticket: call it in at least 2 working days before the old one ends.

trench.text: Federal OSHA covers private crews here: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

sources.what: Ameren Missouri, Aug 7 2025: past 21 days “a new 811 ticket is required”
2025 SB 133, section 319.025 (21-day life, in force Aug 28, 2025)

NM.name: New Mexico

notice.text: Give notice 2 working days ahead, not counting the notice day. Operators have 2 full working days to mark.

life.text: Marks are good for 15 working days from the end of the notice period.

NM.renew: Not done in 15 working days: request a new locate for the work that is left, 2 working days ahead. Wide-area tickets must be reaffirmed every 15 working days.
NM.tol_text: Within 18 inches either side of a mark, expose the line by hand or vacuum first.
NM.white_text: Pre-mark the actual dig site in white in towns. Outside towns, pre-mark or give GPS points.
NM.emergency: Emergency locates: marked as soon as practical, ideally within 2 hours.

trench.text: NM OSHA adopts the federal rule: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

sources.what: NM811 Pipeline Safety book 2019, p. 19 (not done in 15 working days: a new standard locate)

NC.name: North Carolina

notice.text: Call at least 3 full working days before the start date.

life.text: A notice expires 28 calendar days after the work start date. The app counts from the first legal dig day.

NC.renew: Past 28 days, give a new notice the same way as the first: at least 3 full working days ahead.
NC.tol_text: 24 inches applies only to oil, gas transmission and electric transmission lines (no mechanized digging).
NC.white_text: Premark in white when the area can’t be identified from the notice.

trench.text: State OSHA plan. Federal OSHA’s 5 ft rule is the floor; we have not checked whether this plan is stricter.

sources.what: N.C.G.S. 87-122(a) (a later notice is given the same way as the first)

SC.name: South Carolina

notice.text: Operators have 3 full working days to mark, not counting the call day.

life.text: A normal ticket is good for 15 working days from its start time.

SC.renew: Send an Extension any time before the ticket expires: same number, 15 more working days, no new marks. Marks gone: ask for a Remark (new number; operators have 3 full working days).
SC.tol_text: 24 inches each side of the mark, plus half the diameter if known.
SC.white_text: Pre-mark in white when the site can’t be clearly identified.
SC.emergency: Emergency: exempt from the notice rule, but notify SC811 and the operators as soon as practicable.

trench.text: State OSHA plan. Federal OSHA’s 5 ft rule is the floor; we have not checked whether this plan is stricter.

sources.what: S.C. Code 58-36-60(B) as amended, in force May 22, 2026
SC811 Excavator Web Tickets Manual, 2026 (an Extension keeps the number, adds 15 working days)

SD.name: South Dakota

notice.text: Give notice at least 48 hours ahead. The 48 hours start 12:01 AM the next day and skip weekends and state holidays (2026 law).

life.text: Marks are good while clearly visible, but not more than 21 calendar days from the start date on the ticket. The app counts from the first legal dig day.

SD.renew: Update the ticket before the 21 days end. No updates more than 90 days after the first start date. The app’s Renew-by date uses the first-call wait: no source names a day.
SD.tol_text: Marks within 18 inches of the facility; keep 18 inches between marks and machine teeth.

trench.text: Federal OSHA covers private crews here: protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652).

WY.name: Wyoming

notice.text: Call at least 2 full business days and not more than 14 business days before digging.

start.text: Call no more than 14 business days before work starts.

life.text: For longer jobs, renew the notice at least once every 14 business days.

WY.renew: On a job longer than 14 business days, give notice again at least once every 14 business days. The app’s Renew-by date uses the first-call wait: no source names a day.
WY.tol_text: Marks within 24 inches of the facility.
WY.emergency: Emergency digging is exempt from the time limits.

trench.text: State OSHA plan. Federal OSHA’s 5 ft rule is the floor; we have not checked whether this plan is stricter.
